svg.title: The bill vector is the transpose form applied to the selected zero-fluctuation strains, with their original scaling. Finite matrix-vector multiplication compares it. The protected mean is minus the transpose window-column matrix applied to this bill; hence it compares as asserted above. Its scaled stationary defect is the plate times this mean plus the bill, multiplied by −√β, and therefore compares as well. The positive common coupling limit is guaranteed by the lower coupling-window endpoint; taking square roots and reciprocal scales is consequently valid.
